text: A build's own check that owns internal/verify gets an hour, 55 minutes of it for its tests, where #498's plan gave it 25 and 20 (#883). A limit is there to end a run that hangs, not to fail one that's working. internal/verify's tests are the acceptance tests of every Python plan so far, each of which stages and gates a fixture application several times. With internal/plumbing's, two sandboxes at once took 9 minutes 28 on 2026-11-02, 15 minutes 11 on 11-05 and 20 minutes 35 on 11-12, when one of the two failed on time. internal/verify's alone took 17 minutes on 11-13, and the nine packages #857's plan touches took 24. So a build that touched both packages couldn't finish its own check, a draft had timed out on 11-06 (#669), and #857's plan was waiting to be ratified with no chance of being built. The rule is #498's still: only a check that owns the exact package gets the longer limit, overrides only shorten it, and a direct build's tool timer follows it, now 61 minutes 15 seconds. The real-image check asks each of two simultaneous runs to finish with a tenth of its hour to spare, and says what each had. What the tests cost is what grows, and #893 is to make them cheaper.
